title: Indicators and methods for assessing acoustical preferences and needs of students in educational buildings: A review
review_question:
1. What are the indicators that have to be considered to evaluate the acoustical quality taking into account students' acoustical preferences and needs?
2. What are the methods that are used for measuring and assessing these indicators?
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Studies in the domain of soundscape and acoustical environment considering occupant-related indicators in an indoor environment, acoustical environment with one or more effects (positive and/or negative) on individuals' (and students') physiological health, psychological health, performance, and preferences, and cross-modal perception of acoustics with other IEQ-factors. Excluded studies focused only on urban soundscape, objective measurements without occupant-related indicators, or impact on subjects with hearing impairment.

synthesis_conclusions: Acoustical quality significantly influences students' preferences, needs, and well-being in educational buildings, with different students having different preferences and needs.

It is crucial to consider occupant-related indicators (physiological and psychological) when optimizing acoustical quality in educational buildings, as current guidelines primarily focus on dose-related and building-related indicators.
Previous studies demonstrate that dose-related indicators significantly affect occupant-related indicators, highlighting the importance of a comprehensive approach.

The review identifies a comprehensive set of occupant-related (physiological, psychological, demographical), dose-related (acoustical, other IEQ factors), and building-related indicators for assessing acoustical preferences and needs.

Objective measurements at human and environmental levels, soundwalks, questionnaires, interviews, binaural measurements, playing sound stimuli, and building checklists are identified as key methods for investigation.

A holistic approach considering all three categories of indicators (occupant, environmental, and building) is essential for assessing health and comfort in indoor environments and for identifying students' acoustical preferences and needs.
evidence_gaps: Occupant-related indicators (physiological and psychological) are rarely mentioned in acoustical guidelines for educational buildings.
Students' acoustical preferences and needs are rarely investigated by considering occupant-related indicators (both physiological and psychological) in previous studies.
Dose-related indicators of other IEQ factors and building-related indicators are rarely taken into account in previous studies.
The cross-modal perception between acoustical quality and lighting/visual comfort was not widely examined in previous studies.
Few studies have considered building-related indicators.
Almost none of the reviewed studies considered students' acoustical preferences or needs in educational buildings.
Soundwalk was only applied in one study on a study environment (public library) among the reviewed studies.
limitations: The summarized indicators and methods are limited to the 44 selected studies reviewed.
The review is limited to studies on indoor acoustics and soundscape regarding students in schools and universities (undergraduate and graduate).
The minimum age of students in these studies was 8 years old, and the maximum age was 34 years old.
Soundwalk was only applied in one study on a study environment (public library) among the reviewed studies.
